key_facts: NVIDIA Cosmos는 6개의 오픈 모델 리더보드에서 **상위 5위권**을 기록
Porsche는 Volkswagen Group 브랜드 전반의 공유 AV 데이터 플라이휠을 주도하며, Voxel51을 통해 Cosmos Data Factory를 사용해 **물리적 시험 주행을 최대 90% 감소, 개발 주기를 최대 85% 단축**할 것으로 예상
ANYbotics는 Cosmos Data Factory 블루프린트로 1,500개 이상의 합성 비디오 클립을 생성해 산업 점검 로봇의 액체 유출 등 변화 인식 학습에 활용
MicroAGI는 Cosmos 3를 자기중심적 조작(egocentric manipulation) 영상으로 post-training하고 **320억 파라미터 reasoner를 80억 파라미터 Nano 모델로 정확도 손실 없이 증류**
Cosmos Data Factory는 Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation, Image Attribute Augmentation, Event Video Generation, Defect Image Generation, Video Data Augmentation 등 5개 블루프린트 제공
summary_data.why_matters: NVIDIA는 데이터 큐레이션부터 모델 학습·최적화·시뮬레이션 평가까지 **물리적 AI(Physical AI) 개발 전체 파이프라인을 Cosmos 플랫폼으로 통합**하며 월드 모델 생태계의 표준 인프라로 자리매김하려 한다. Porsche·Volkswagen Group, ANYbotics, Ultralytics 등 실제 산업 고객의 적용 사례가 구체적 수치로 제시되어 플랫폼의 실효성을 입증한다.
summary_data.subject_angle: NVIDIA는 GPU 하드웨어 공급자에서 벗어나 **자율주행·로봇용 합성 데이터 생성 및 월드 모델 학습 전 과정을 아우르는 소프트웨어·플랫폼 기업으로 포지션을 확장**하고 있으며, Azure·CoreWeave·Nebius 등 멀티클라우드 배포로 생태계 락인을 강화한다.
summary_data.focus_angle: Porsche와 Volkswagen Group은 Cosmos Data Factory로 **실도로 시험 주행을 최대 90% 줄이는 AV 데이터 플라이휠**을 구축하고 있어, OEM의 자율주행 개발 비용·시간 구조를 바꿀 잠재력이 있으며, ANYbotics와 MicroAGI의 사례는 산업용 휴머노이드·조작 로봇의 world model 기반 학습이 실제 현장(공장·창고)에 적용되기 시작했음을 보여준다.

cards.body: To help developers rapidly build world models , which help physical AI systems understand and simulate the real world, NVIDIA has expanded the Cosmos platform with new training tools, simulation checkpoints and Cosmos Data Factory blueprints. Ranking top five on six different open models leaderboards, the NVIDIA Cosmos platform gives world model builders the frontier open models — as well as data, training and optimization tools and recipes — to scale training data, adapt models, test behavior and optimize for performance before deployment. Build Better Training Data Building world models begins with multimodal, multisensory data. NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory brings together the tools and skills for labeling, curating, augmenting and evaluating data at scale for training physical AI. Cosmos Curator, a GPU-accelerated solution for curating video training datasets, has now added support for multimodal multisensory inputs and processing blocks. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Cosmos Data Factory now offers the following five cloud-native blueprints and is available through GitHub , Microsoft Azure , Nebius and CoreWeave : Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation: Curates and labels driving data, then adds synthetic examples of hard-to-capture scenarios to expand training coverage. Image Attribute Augmentation: Varies object appearance to improve image search. Event Video Generation: Turns still images into synthetic videos of rare or unsafe events. Defect Image Generation: Generates printed circuit board, metal and glass defect images for inspection models. Video Data Augmentation: Changes weather and lighting in existing footage while preserving scene structure. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/CDF-visual-Oct20.mp4 Cosmos Data Factory accelerates data curation, processing and synthetic data generation with agentic skills. Companies are already putting Cosmos Data Factory blueprints to work to speed their physical AI development workflows. Porsche is leading the development of a shared AV data flywheel across Volkswagen Group brands, using Cosmos Data Factory through Voxel51 on Microsoft Azure. This is expected to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shorten development cycle times by up to 85%. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Porche-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 Porsche searching and augmenting autonomous vehicle data footage in Voxel51, powered by Cosmos Data Factory. ANYbotics generated over 1,500 synthetic video clips with Cosmos Data Factory blueprints, curating real-world data and validating outputs with Encord’s platform, to train its industrial-inspection robots to recognize liquid spills and other changes between facility visits. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ANYbotics-Cosmos-Data-Factory.mp4 ANYbotic s generating anomaly clips with Encord powered by NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory. key_facts: LG이노텍이 **엔비디아와 휴머노이드용 비전 센싱, 로봇 핸즈 등 피지컬 AI 센싱 솔루션을 공동 개발**
엔비디아의 센서 데이터 전송 기술과 LG이노텍의 카메라·라이다(LiDAR)·레이더(Radar) 기술 결합 방식
10월 20일(현지시간) 독일 베를린 'GTC 베를린'에서 공개, 10월 22일 국내 발표
공개된 솔루션은 3메가픽셀(MP) 카메라 모듈과 멀티모달 비전 시스템(MVS)
**엔비디아의 Holoscan Sensor Bridge(HSB) 기술**을 적용, 카메라·센서 데이터를 CPU를 거치지 않고 전송하는 방식(본문 일부 확인)
summary_data.why_matters: **휴머노이드 로봇 시장에서 센서-컴퓨팅 통합 레퍼런스 아키텍처 경쟁이 본격화**되는 가운데, NVIDIA가 자사 플랫폼(HSB)을 중심으로 Tier1 부품업체를 끌어들여 생태계를 확장하는 사례다. 한국 부품사(LG Innotek)가 NVIDIA 로봇 생태계에 공식 파트너로 편입된 것은 글로벌 공급망 재편 신호로 해석될 수 있다.
summary_data.subject_angle: **NVIDIA는 HSB 기술을 매개로 카메라·LiDAR·Radar 등 이종 센서 벤더를 자사 로봇/피지컬 AI 플랫폼에 종속시키는 전략**을 취하고 있으며, 이는 데이터센터 중심 GPU 사업을 넘어 로보틱스 하드웨어 생태계 장악력을 넓히려는 행보다.
summary_data.focus_angle: **휴머노이드 OEM 및 로봇 제조사 입장에서는 NVIDIA-LG Innotek 조합이 비전·센싱 모듈의 표준 레퍼런스가 될 가능성**이 있어, 향후 로봇 핸즈·휴머노이드 플랫폼 설계 시 HSB 기반 센서 통합이 사실상 기본 선택지로 자리잡을 수 있다.

Stripe Radar는 NVIDIA GPU 가속 Ray Data로 **데이터 파이프라인 42배 가속, 92% 비용 절감**

summary_data.subject_angle: NVIDIA는 GPU 하드웨어뿐 아니라 cuDF, Dynamo-Triton, Nemotron, Kumo 등 **자체 소프트웨어·모델 스택**을 금융 규제 산업에 깊이 통합시켜, 오픈 모델 생태계의 표준 가속 인프라로 포지셔닝하고 있다.

cards.body: At GTC Berlin, banks, payment companies and financial data providers are showing what production-scale intelligence looks like — built on NVIDIA accelerated computing, powered by open weight models and running on their own infrastructure. Revolut is rebuilding its technology stack on a single foundation model PRAGMA , powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Using the NVIDIA cuDF toolkit and Dynamo-Triton software on NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs , Revolut is scaling PRAGMA in production, servicing an initial 80 million customers and engineered to scale 3x. “Revolut processes billions of transactions — the opportunity was always there, but the question was whether foundation models could operate at that scale and across domains. PRAGMA answers that,” said Pavel Nesterov, head of AI at Revolut. “Built in collaboration with NVIDIA, it’s the clearest proof yet that the gap between a research breakthrough and a production banking system can be closed.” Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Training on Accelerated Infrastructure Starling Bank , the first bank to train an agentic model on U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure, has developed “Starling Intelligence” — the intelligence layer that underpins its AI capability — on Civo’s U.K. cloud using the bank’s own transaction data. Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM , a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable intelligence — accelerated with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and improving efficiency across bank-wide use cases. SBS launched a banking sovereign intelligence platform so banks can run generative and agentic models without their data leaving their own walls. Open Models at a Fraction of the Cost Open weight models give European financial institutions proprietary intelligence built on data they own, at costs they control. NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform is the engine running beneath them. Neobank bunq’s agentic assistant Finn now runs on open weight models. Powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deploying on Nebius matches the quality of leading closed models at 60% of the cost per answer. NatWest is building technology designed to recognize the full range of British accents, dialects and financial terminology, developed with NVIDIA’s speech models, including Nemotron 3.5 ASR. Modulr is building specialized models for distinct parts of payment operations, based on the NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B open model. Santander is an early adopter of the new NVIDIA Kumo family of open weight foundation models for structured financial data, using them to build specialized intelligence for core banking workloads. Accelerated Computing Transforms Financial Research LSEG is working with NVIDIA to help financial institutions analyze large volumes of historical tick data up to 10x faster with the Polars GPU engine , accelerated by NVIDIA cuDF on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. summary_data.korean_summary: NVIDIA가 Shopify, Zooplus, Photoroom, Omi, L'Oréal, Mirakl, Otto Group 등 유럽 리테일 기업들과 협력해 오픈 모델 기반 에이전틱 커머스와 물리적 AI(디지털 트윈·시뮬레이션)를 통해 추론 비용 절감과 창고 자동화를 실현하고 있음을 발표했다.

action.action: 유럽 리테일 기업들과 협력하여 NVIDIA Nemotron, Megatron Bridge, NeMo RL, Omniverse 등을 활용한 에이전틱 커머스 및 물리적 AI(디지털 트윈) 솔루션 적용
action.scope: 유럽 리테일·이커머스·뷰티 산업 (Shopify, Zooplus, Photoroom, Omi, L'Oréal, Mirakl, Otto Group 등)

key_facts: Shopify는 NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning을 post-train하여 **서빙 비용 90% 절감, 응답속도 7배 향상**을 달성했으며, NVIDIA NeMo RL과 Megatron Bridge를 활용함
Shopify는 NVIDIA CCluster vLLM 최적화로 5개 추가 use case에서 4.5배 빠른 성능, 최대 12배 낮은 추론 비용을 달성
Zooplus는 Infosys 및 NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever 기반으로 AWS 환경에서 **86% 검색 정확도**를 달성한 프로토타입을 구축
Photoroom은 Vestiaire Collective에 배포되어 하루 약 40,000개 이미지를 70개국에서 처리하며, 이를 통해 상품 판매율 5% 상승, 조회수 3~7% 증가
Otto Group은 Reply와 NVIDIA Omniverse 라이브러리를 활용해 Google Cloud 기반 자율 창고 시스템을 독일 Haldensleben 최대 풀필먼트 센터로 확장
summary_data.why_matters: 유럽 주요 리테일·이커머스·뷰티 기업들이 NVIDIA의 오픈 모델 post-training 및 물리적 AI 시뮬레이션 기술을 실제 운영 환경에 적용해 **비용 절감과 정확도 개선을 동시에 달성**하고 있음을 보여준다. 이는 NVIDIA의 AI 인프라가 디지털 커머스뿐 아니라 물류·창고 자동화 영역까지 확장되고 있음을 시사한다.
summary_data.subject_angle: NVIDIA는 Nemotron, Omniverse, ALCHEMI, Dynamo 등 자사 풀스택 소프트웨어·하드웨어 생태계를 유럽 리테일 기업들에 침투시켜 **에이전틱 커머스와 물리적 AI 양쪽에서 플랫폼 지배력을 강화**하고 있으며, 주권형 AI 수요(Mirakl의 Scaleway 활용 사례)에도 대응하고 있다.

headlines.body: Weather forecasts shape more than daily plans; timely weather information is crucial for energy producers, insurers and transport operators to plan around changing conditions. A global forecast can show a storm taking shape, but decisions about solar farms, shipping routes or insured property depend on what happens locally. NVIDIA Earth-2 gives developers and researchers a family of open AI models and tools they can customize with their own data. Running on NVIDIA computing, these technologies support global weather prediction, detailed regional forecasts and environmental research. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements StormScope EU is the latest model to join Earth-2 — a regional version of the StormScope model for short-term forecasting, trained over Europe weather and climate data. It uses EUMETSAT satellite observations to predict evolving cloud conditions across 16 Meteosat channels at 10-minute intervals. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing a live StormScope EU pipeline in an interactive weather demo built in partnership with Earthmover . The demo uses Earth2Studio to run forecasts and Earthmover’s data platform to manage and serve the real-time results, which are updated as soon as new satellite observations come in, every 10 minutes. Earthmover serves these results as map tiles, letting visitors explore predictions across Europe without downloading entire datasets. Developers can combine Earth-2 models in workflows tailored to regional needs, using StormScope for short-term forecasting and CorrDiff to add local detail to coarser weather data. Developers can also pick up these model architectures and train them for new environmental applications such as air-quality modeling. The open source NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo framework provides training and customization tools so teams can build applications that incorporate proprietary data and domain expertise to meet regional needs. Organizations building on Earth-2 capabilities include: AXA is using NVIDIA Earth-2’s FourCastNet 3 to study regional cyclone risk beyond the historical record across more than 1,000 simulated seasons, generating insights that can inform risk assessments and help customers target prevention efforts. Vaisala Xweather is combining Earth-2 with its proprietary observations , lightning data and forecasting expertise to enhance its weather intelligence platforms for government, energy, maritime, transportation and insurance customers. headlines.body: T-Mobile has paired with Nvidia and Nokia to complete what the companies claim to be the world's first AI-RAN voice call. The call was completed from a commercial cell site in Bellevue, Washington, where US carrier T-Mobile is headquartered. The call was carried out over T-Mobile’s live production network using Nokia Massive MIMO radio, Nokia 5G anyRAN software, and server infrastructure built on Nvidia Aerial RAN Computer platform. In a blog post, Nokia noted that the site was connected to commercial 5G core and commercial user equipment. It builds on comments made by T-Mobile's CTO, John Saw at Mobile World Congress, that the operator was hopeful it would have trial units to play with this year, when Nokia mapped out its AI-RAN masterplan, with support from Nvidia and a clutch of carriers, including T-Mobile According to the vendor, the voice call is significant as it means that AI-RAN is moving out of controlled lab environments and into live operator network, with real spectrum and commercial network infrastructure. The next phase of field trials will extend to new AI-for-RAN algorithms and AI workloads running alongside RAN on a shared accelerated computing platform. Nokia has big ambitions to push AI-RAN, and sees the technology as a key cog in helping to evolve the RAN into a more software-defined, AI-native platform, ahead of the 6G era. "AI-RAN represents an important evolution of the radio network. Nokia’s vision is to evolve the RAN into an increasingly software-defined, AI-native platform, creating a common foundation for future AI-enabled services and the evolution toward 6G," said Pallavi Mahajan, chief technology and AI officer, Nokia. "With AI-RAN, we are on a path to 2x spectral efficiency, an ambition that puts more capacity from the same spectrum at the heart of what comes next." The company's vision around implementing AI into the radio access network is one of the main reasons the vendor has formed closer ties to GPU giant Nvidia. The two companies first penned an agreement to develop AI-ready RAN solutions back in 2024, long before Nvidia became an investor in the vendor. But mobile carriers have also been looking into AI-RAN during this timeframe too, including T-Mobile, which announced an AI-RAN Innovation Center in Bellevue back in September 2024. Earlier this year, the three companies also announced they are working with other partners to deliver physical AI applications over distributed Edge AI networks. "The next phase of field trials will build on this milestone, exploring additional spectrum bands and the ability to support AI inferencing workloads alongside RAN functions. Each step brings us closer to understanding how AI-RAN can deliver meaningful benefits in real-world network environments and ultimately operate at scale," added Pallavi. headlines.body: Infineon has partnered with Nvidia to develop gallium nitride (GaN) power conversion technology for 800 VDC data center architectures. The German chipmaker announced the tie-up at Nvidia’s GTC Berlin developer conference, building on a May 2025 agreement detailed in October 2025 that focused on serviceable, hot-swappable 800 VDC server racks. The latest agreement will focus on developing high-voltage intermediate bus converters (IBCs). IBCs step down the main bus voltage feeding accelerator cards to a lower-voltage rail, allowing downstream stages to generate the core and point-of-load rails AI processors need. Infineon said the multi-stage approach reduces distribution losses while meeting limits on board area, thermals, and uptime. It added that 800 VDC is being introduced alongside existing AC and lower-voltage DC architectures as an additional option for higher-density compute. Infineon claims GaN switches faster than silicon and with lower losses, enabling switching frequencies up to 1MHz at the IBC stage. The company asserts this lets magnetics and passives shrink, increasing power density and reducing board height. The company said this matters as rack power levels approach the megawatt range. Infineon's GaN portfolio covers 800V-to-50V, 800V-to-12V, and 800V-to-6V conversion. Infineon pairs the devices with its PSoC Control C3 and EiceDRIVER product families to offer full IBC system solutions. It also offers IBC solutions in silicon and silicon carbide. “AI is fundamentally reshaping the demands we place on power infrastructure, and semiconductors are at the heart of solving that challenge,” said Jochen Hanebeck, CEO, Infineon Technologies AG. “Our collaboration with Nvidia on 800V power architectures shows what is possible when deep semiconductor expertise meets the pace of innovation required by AI. Gallium nitride-based system solutions are a key enabler of this next generation of data centers, and Infineon is proud to help power the AI era from grid to core.” The agreement follows a deal with Estonian power and storage systems supplier Skeleton Technologies last month, which will see the companies jointly explore and develop advanced architectures for the entire AI data center power chain, from the grid to the facility itself. This will include Solid State Transformers for medium-voltage AC-to-high-voltage DC conversion. Infineon is one of Europe's largest semiconductor manufacturers. Spun out of Siemens in 1999, the company specializes in power electronics, automotive microcontrollers, sensors, and security chips. Recently, it increased its research and development in power infrastructure for the data center sector, partnering with Korean electrical equipment manufacturer LS Electric to develop direct current power infrastructure for the AI data center market earlier this year.

headlines.body: Dell Technologies has expanded its Dell AI Factory with Nvidia product portfolio, adding a Vera CPU server and rack, and a rack-scale inference system built on Groq 3 Language Processing Units (LPUs), to its hardware lineup. In a statement, Dell said its AI Factory platform has surpassed 6,500 customers, up from 5,000 in the previous quarter. The Dell PowerEdge M9882 comprises 256 Nvidia Vera CPUs in a single 48U rack, allowing companies to maximize data center power and cooling capacity by separating out CPU compute from GPU clusters. Dell said the rack has been purpose-built to support agentic AI workloads, and offers orchestration, tool use, code execution and evaluation, which can run alongside GPU infrastructure for model inference. Meanwhile, the Dell PowerEdge R8822 server is an air-cooled, two-socket Nvidia Vera CPU offering that fits into standard 19-inch rack environments. Like its rack-scale counterpart, the R8822 has also been optimized for agentic AI workloads and can run reinforcement learning, data processing, and analytics, with support for up to four double-wide GPUs to accelerate AI and compute-intensive tasks. Finally, Dell has launched the PowerEdge XE9810, the first offering from the company to feature Groq 3 LPUs. Featuring 16 direct-liquid-cooled compute trays, Dell did not provide details on the number of LPUs per tray, but said that the server functions as “an ideal disaggregated complement to existing GPU clusters,” purpose-built for the high-throughput demands of production agentic AI. “Enterprises used to think about AI infrastructure as an IT budget question, but that's changed,” said Michael Dell, CEO of Dell Technologies. “AI infrastructure is no longer a cost center. It's a value creation center. Companies are expanding and reallocating budgets because AI infrastructure drives growth, productivity and competitive advantage. Together with Nvidia, we are giving enterprises the integrated platforms they need to move agentic AI from experimentation to results, on infrastructure they own and control.” The Dell PowerEdge R8822 will be available this month, with the M9882 and XE9810 coming in Q1 2027.

headlines.body: Launched today, NVIDIA Minerva is an AIOps platform built to help teams find problems earlier and keep AI factories productive. It brings together telemetry from infrastructure and AI workloads, then applies purpose-built AI models to turn that data into timely, actionable insight. AI factories are among the most complex operations in the world, with vast numbers of GPUs working across high-speed networks to train models and serve AI applications. At that scale, a single degraded component can slow an entire job. The warning signs may be easy to miss, such as a GPU running hotter than its peers or an NVMe drive losing performance under load. The platform focuses on AI factory yield, a measure of the useful work infrastructure produces through GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and token production. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Delivering a Dynamic View of an AI Factory Traditional monitoring tools often divide the data center into separate views. Networking, compute, site reliability and machine learning teams each see a different part of the operation. Minerva connects those signals across NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and workloads. With these signals, Minerva builds a dynamic knowledge graph that logically maps the infrastructure — GPUs, SuperNICs, switches and cables — and the jobs running on it. This context helps operators trace a slow training job to the component affecting it, even across a factory with hundreds of thousands of GPUs. It analyzes billions of data points per hour using supervised and unsupervised machine learning. It learns normal behavior, detects previously unseen anomalies, predicts emerging failures and correlates related events based on the factory’s topology. Instead of sending every symptom to an operator, it can group an event storm into a focused incident with a likely root cause. Minerva comes with a native AI assistant and connects to external agentic AI tools. This adds a natural-language interface grounded in live telemetry. Operators can investigate cluster health and receive recommended remediation through conversation. Teams can keep a person in the loop to manually implement fixes or connect Minerva to automation through infrastructure application programming interfaces and external systems. Instead of dealing with a blizzard of alerts, Minerva aggregates related problems into a single actionable item. This allows AIOps teams to move from reactive to proactive maintenance. headlines.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC Thursday that a surplus of memory supply is unlikely by 2029, despite a sell-off in memory stocks over the past week amid concerns about oversupply and weakening demand. "One of the things that's really great about memory is that you can always use more of it," Huang told CNBC's Arjun Kharpal in a wide-ranging interview on the sidelines of the company's GTC Berlin conference. He added that HBM, a type of random access memory, or RAM, will be used for years to come. "We're the first company in the world to put LPDDR memory — what goes into your cell phones — into the world's data centers, and it's enabled us to deliver performance that's twice as energy efficient as anything in the world today, and so we're going to continue to use abundant amounts of them as well," he added. Memory stocks have taken a battering in the past week after an opinion column published in a prominent South Korean publication on Oct. 15 urged the country's government to brace for a deceleration in the AI boom. The column cited two experts who said they expect to see a "flood of new supply," which will turn the memory market "into a red ocean" in 2029, per CNBC's translation. "The supercycle could be over, and the industry could enter a downturn," by 2029, they wrote. Memory is a core component of Nvidia's chips, and a glut of supply could push prices lower and hit profit margins for the companies that make the product, such as SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron. SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk responded to the article at the time, saying that China "will be making a LOT of RAM in 2028." The memory selloff was also driven by China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, which announced new design architecture that could lead to greater efficiencies. The announcement added to investor concern that CXMT could take market share from rivals SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron. "We're open-minded," Huang said Thursday when asked about whether he plans to partner with CXMT and use its memory product. "We work with Chinese companies; just about the whole world works with Chinese companies in the supply chain somewhere." "China is incredible at the fundamental infrastructure technology, and no country collectively is better at manufacturing than China, and so we have to take their capabilities very seriously," he added. headlines.body: Nvidia is reportedly in talks to inject private investment in neocloud Firmus after the company dropped plans for an initial public offering (IPO). As per a report from The Information, citing people familiar with the matter, the investment could be to the tune of several hundreds of millions of dollars. Bloomberg previously reported that Firmus was seeking between $2 billion and $3bn in private funding following the drop of its IPO, in which the company had been hoping to secure as much as $5bn. DCD has contacted Firmus and Nvidia for comment. Firmus backed out of plans for the IPO earlier this month, stating that following its decision to reduce the price of its IPO, “the board therefore concluded that proceeding with the offer was not in the best interests of the company and its shareholders. Firmus will now pursue capital from the private markets and consider alternative public and private market options.” Most recently, Firmus raised $2bn via an equity sale in August 2026, following a previous $505m equity investment round in April. The August round gave the company a post-money valuation of more than $10.5bn. Nvidia is an existing investor in the company, having participated in previous rounds. The companies are also working together on a 170,000 GPU cluster in Batam, Indonesia, in an agreement that will see Firmus procure Nvidia AI infrastructure through 2034, and provide Nvidia-powered cloud services. Firmus was also one of the early participants in Nvidia's credit-sharing agreements in which it acts as a backstop in return for a cut of revenues. According to The Information, thus far Nvidia has invested some $170bn in neoclouds and other large customers, including credit guarantees to help them raise the debt necessary for their AI infrastructure buildouts. Firmus’ major investors include Blackstone, Coatue Management and Jane Street. Nvidia has participated in Firmus’ last three funding rounds. The company has raised more than $13bn in total, including around $10bn in debt. Shortly before dropping its IPO, news that Firmus and CDC Data Centres had gone their separate ways emerged due to Firmus' planned expansion in Asia. CDC CEO Greg Boorer said: "We’re certainly not planning on doing 1.6GW of rollout with them because they made other choices regarding doing their own data center developments, which is slightly different to what we envisaged," and similarly pointed out that Firmus would need to raise tens of billions of dollars to scale according to its plans. headlines.body: Two months after leaving OpenAI, Chris Malone, the former head of data centers at the AI giant, has joined Nvidia as vice president, DSX Platform. Announcing his new role on LinkedIn, Malone said that after spending a few weeks with the team, he’s “even more convinced of the opportunity ahead.” Malone spent 18 months at OpenAI, joining from Meta, where he spent nearly five years as a distinguished engineer. Prior to that, he spent nearly 12 years at Google, focused on the company's data center infrastructure and IT hardware R&D. At OpenAI, he worked alongside head of infrastructure and fellow Meta alum Keith Heyde, until his departure earlier this year. Peter Hoeschele, who ran the Stargate joint venture, also left around that time, bringing several AI infrastructure senior leaders with him. The team was consolidated under Sachin Katti, but the former Intel exec himself left earlier this month. Former xAI lead Uday Ruddarraju is now in charge of OpenAI's infrastructure and compute business, and has brought a number of xAI staffers to OpenAI. Among them is Brent Mayo, who has been named head of data center build and delivery. “AI is fundamentally changing how data centers are designed, built, and operated. The scale, power density, cooling requirements, and speed of deployment demand new approaches across the industry,” Malone wrote in his post. “I see tremendous potential for DSX to help meet that challenge. By bringing computing, power, cooling, and operations together in a common platform, we can help partners build AI factories faster, use energy more efficiently, and get more useful computing from every megawatt.“ First unveiled in March 2026 at GTC San Jose, the DSX AI Factory Platform is a guide to building data centers that support its latest CPU-GPU racks and Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and storage. This week, Nvidia claimed that the DSX Platform will allow customers to build AI data centers that minimize the amount of water consumed by cooling technologies by up to 100 percent, whilst also utilizing up to 30 percent less power for the same output. To support the platform, Nvidia launched DSX POD at GTC Berlin this week, a modular version of the reference design for Vera Rubin-powered AI data centers. Built in containers that have been integrated and validated ahead of delivery, the company said the units can be connected to a prepared site’s power, cooling, networking, and other supporting infrastructure to reduce deployment time from six months to 14 days.

stage1.korean_summary: 인피니언이 NVIDIA와 고전압 중간버스컨버터 개발 협력을 확대하여 GaN 기반 전력반도체 솔루션을 공급한다.

headlines.body: 인피니언이 엔비디아와 인공지능(AI) 데이터센터용 800V 직류(DC) 전력변환 기술 개발 협력을 확대한다. 800V를 서버 보드용 중간 전압으로 낮추는 장치에 쓸 수 있도록 질화갈륨(GaN) 전력반도체와 제어 솔루션을 공급한다. 인피니언은 엔비디아와 고전압 중간버스컨버터(HV IBC:High-Voltage Intermediate Bus Converter) 개발 협력을 확대한다고 21일(현지시간) 밝혔다. 이는 지난해 협력 발표의 연장이다. 당시 800V 서버 랙의 보호회로가 중심이었다. IBC는 서버로 들어온 높은 전압을 보드 내부 중간 전압으로 낮추는 장치다. 이 전압은 다음 단계에서 그래픽처리장치(GPU) 코어 전압으로 한 번 더 변환된다. 인피니언은 800V를 50V와 12V, 6V로 낮추는 구성을 지원한다. 800VDC가 주목받는 이유는 GPU 전력 소비 증가 때문이다. AI 데이터센터는 GPU를 다량으로 배치하면서 랙당 전력이 메가와트급으로 올라가고 있다. 엔비디아는 기존 교류(AC)와 저전압 직류 방식과 별도로 랙까지 800V 직류를 그대로 보내는 설계를 추진하며 관련 생태계를 조성하고 있다. 이 경우 전력 손실과 배선 규모가 줄어든다. GaN 전력반도체는 실리콘보다 스위칭이 빠르고 변환 손실이 적다. 인피니언은 최대 1MHz 스위칭 주파수를 구현할 수 있다고 설명했다. 스위칭이 빨라지면 변압기와 코일 등 주변 부품은 작은 것을 쓸 수 있다. 같은 공간에서 더 많은 전력을 처리할 수 있어 공간이 제한적인 고밀도 AI 서버에 유리하다. 발열도 줄어든다. 인피니언은 GaN 전력반도체와 PSoC 컨트롤 C3 컨트롤러, EiceDRIVER 제품군을 묶어 IBC용 시스템 솔루션으로 공급한다. 요헨 하나벡(Jochen Hanebeck) 인피니언 최고경영자(CEO)는 "GaN 기반 시스템 솔루션은 차세대 데이터센터를 구현하는 핵심 기술"이라며 "인피니언은 그리드에서 코어까지 AI 시대에 필요한 전력을 공급하는 데 기여하고 있다"고 말했다.

Training used the locally verified 402-episode dataset. The saved training configuration specifies a 40,000-step cosine learning-rate schedule, with this checkpoint captured at step 15,000. The learning rate increases linearly from zero to a peak of `1e-4` over the first 2,000 steps (`warmup_ratio = 0.05`), then follows cosine decay to zero over steps 2,000–40,000 without restarts. At step 15,000, during the decay phase, the training log records a learning rate of approximately `7.38e-5`. The repository name identifies the 40,000-step cosine schedule and the checkpoint saved at step 15,000; the schedule was not compressed to end at step 15,000. Isaac `GR00T N1.7-3B` is the medium-sized version of the model, built using pretrained vision and language encoders. It uses a flow-matching action transformer to model a chunk of actions conditioned on vision, language, and proprioception. This model is distributed in Safetensors format, with three weight shards and an index, accompanied by model and processor configurations and normalization statistics. (Note: For overlapping speech, this model is trained to preserve the main speaker while suppressing other speakers.) NVIDIA NemotronLabs RE-USE-laughter was developed by NVIDIA as a part of RE-USE. This model is ready for commercial use. ### Performance Comparison with other open-source USE models on the (subsets) of the URGENT 2025 non-blind test set, referenced against original anechoic clean speech. **SBERT**: SpeechBERTScore, **LPS**: Levenshtein Phoneme Similarity, **Spk**: Speaker similarity (ECAPA-TDNN), **CAcc**: Character accuracy of ASR (OWSM v3.1) | Full set | # of parameters | DNSMOS | NISQA | UTMOS | PESQ | STOI | SB
